frames.review_note: v02 fixes the v01 fault: the troop is now small and far down the beach, the foreground is empty shining wet sand, the sun has just cleared the palms on the laterite bluff at left, the sea is at right, and there is wide open sky for the caption. The riders wear white jamas and white turbans with plain upright lances, and a single tiny green turban leads the column. Minor notes, not grounds to reject: the column is a broad front about twelve abreast rather than two or three abreast. The rear ranks are painted as pale, semi-transparent hazy figures between the dark front horses. At print size they read as spray or haze rather than grey horses, but a light edit could darken them if the author objects. The riders wear a diagonal shoulder strap, which matches panels 1.4 and 1.5. v01 is not acceptable: the troop is close and large, filling the frame.

v02 is clean: one dark-bay foreleg in readable anatomy (knee, cannon, fetlock with feathering, then the pastern and hoof sunk in grey slurry), a thin sheet of foam sliding in from the right, and the shore behind is only wet sand, surf and a laterite bluff with palms. There is no building, ship or person. The style is inked, the light is warm dawn, and open sky at upper right takes the caption. The other legs at left are sharper than 'soft', but they are clearly the same horse and harmless. v01 is not acceptable because it shows a European church or fort building on the far shore and is near-photoreal.

v02 is acceptable: a tight dark-bay eye rolled with the white showing, a plain leather bridle, a quilted saddle edge at lower right, and only the edge of a high-wrapped white turban and a bamboo lance shaft at upper left, with no rider face. The setting is the open beach, the laterite bluff with palms and the sea, in the inked style. The upper right is open sky for both captions. Notes: the eye is stylised, with a rounder iris and pupil than a real horse's, but it reads as a wary animal and not a human expression. A small white forehead star at the left edge is fine for a Madurai horse. The tiny background structure on the bluff is a three-pole canopy with a row of small figures and two cook fires, not the one-pole awning with two seated figures of panel 2.2. It is very small and soft, so it is noted, not rejected. v01 is not acceptable: it has stone fort walls behind the horse and is photoreal.

The round 3 fix landed. The sun disc on the left sea horizon and its golden glitter across the waves and wet sand are gone. That part of the sky is now pale blue-grey with soft pink cloud, and the sea and wet sand are cool silver-blue with no reflection. There is no sunburst anywhere. Nothing else got worse. Raza Khan's face, olive-green high-wrapped turban (the only green on the beach), pointed moustache and goatee, and the scar on his anatomical left cheek (our right) all still match his sheet. So do his green drape and the right fist gripping the upright lance at his chest. Every Madurai rider wears a white jama and a white turban and carries a bamboo lance with no pennon. The horses are dark bay, brown or black, with no greys. The surf, the laterite bluff and the palms are unchanged, and there is no ship, building, European or text. Hands and anatomy are sound. Open sky across the upper left (about x 0 to 0.40, y 0 to 0.17) and the upper right (about x 0.55 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.14) leaves room for the caption and both Raza Khan balloons, crossed only by thin lance tips. Minor points, not grounds to reject: the salute reads as a fist on the upright lance at the chest rather than a spear butt pressed to the chest, which was carried over from v02. The horses are not clearly tossing their heads. Several troop horses and Raza's horse have small white stars, which the troop rule allows. v02 is not a backup because it still has the sun rising over the western sea.

v02 is acceptable and matches the commander figure on the Nagoji sheet. He wears a rust-red turban with curls at the nape, a cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, a broad red sash over the shoulder and knotted at the waist, cream trousers, laced boots and a brass-hilted talwar at his hip. He has a thick curled moustache and a clean chin. He rides a plain grey on a padded, quilted Indian cloth saddle with a plain bridle and no horn. He looks past the camera at the riders, cool and appraising. The soft backs of two Madurai riders in white turbans frame the near edge, and the setting is the open beach with sea and a laterite bluff with palms, consistent with panel 1.1 as a reverse angle. Hands and anatomy are sound, and the upper sky is open for the caption. Note only: his ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop rather than a flush stud, matching the sheet, and the author has not yet decided between the two. There is faint shading on the chin, but it reads as clean-shaven. v01 is not acceptable: it shows a fort, ships, Portuguese soldiers in morions and breastplates, and prisoners in rags.

Minor only. Ponnan matches the bible and script: bare-headed, short curly hair, thick moustache, clean chin, dark-brown short jacket, red cloth over his anatomical right shoulder, white mundu hitched with bare knees, on a small dun pony. The Maravar line is bare-headed in short jackets and white mundus, ponies dun and dark brown, no greys. Low angle up at a laterite bluff. Small points: the distant background to the right shows an inland lagoon and hills rather than palms on the bluff; Ponnan and the riders have shoes in their stirrups; one background rider has a beard. Open sky at upper left and upper right takes both captions without covering any face.

v02 fixes v01's failures. v01 was not a long shot and had infantry ranks on the beach. v02 is a true long shot with a small awning in the right third on the laterite bluff. Varma is bare-headed with his hair in a knot to his left, Vaishnavite lines, bare chest, a cream-and-gold cloth and gold necklaces, and his spear leans by the main pole. Ramayyan is thin and receding, in white, with the palm-leaf bundle and stylus. The far Madurai riders wear white turbans, with one green for Raza. The bare-headed Maravar line sits under the palms beside the awning. There are no buildings or text, and the upper-left sky is wide open for the caption. Minor notes, none rejectable: (1) the awning cloth is stretched between a thin left support stick and the main pole, so it is not strictly one-pole; (2) the heat haze shows as shimmer in the wet-sand reflections more than in the air; (3) one far Madurai horse (third from left) reads as a greyish dark brown at tiny scale; (4) the distant Maravar riders look bare-chested with white cross-cloths rather than in short jackets.

v01 is rejected: its brand reads as cursive writing and its jaw has stubble. v02 fixes both. The brand is now one irregular, merged patch of puckered scar tissue on the inner left forearm with no letter shapes. The jaw is clean-shaven, apart from faint skin hatching. It keeps the high over-the-left-shoulder angle, rust-red turban, red sash, talwar hilt, pushed-back cream sleeve, a sound five-digit hand on the reins and the plain grey with a dark mane. The sand in the upper right is open for both captions. Notes: the brand is slightly pinkish, though paler than the skin. The nail ridging is subtle. The ear ornament is a small hanging gold ball rather than a stud (note only, per the author's open decision).

v01 is rejected for the European fort on the headland. v02 removes it: the background is only the beach, surf, palms and the laterite bluff, with the picket line and cook fires far left. The three riders are abreast and face the camera. Raza (left) has the green turban, goatee, green drape and white jama, as on his sheet, rides a dark bay and shows the scar on his anatomical left cheek. Nagoji (centre) has the rust-red turban, clean chin, curled moustache, cream tunic, red sash and boots, and points with his right arm down the beach. Ponnan (right) is bare-headed and curly-haired, in a dark-brown jacket with red cloth over his right shoulder, a white mundu and bare legs, sitting clearly lower on a dun pony. The sky above is open for two balloons. Minor notes: (1) Ponnan's collarless jacket shows a short placket with tiny buttons; (2) a far background pole at the picket line has a small red tip, unreadable as a pennon at print size, and a red cloth canopy stands in the picket camp; (3) Nagoji's earrings are small hanging gold drops (note only); (4) the grey is a light dappled grey, consistent with 2.3.

v01 is rejected for a church and fort on the headland, a red conch banner and green turbans in the troop. v02 removes all three. The troop behind wear white turbans and white jamas and carry plain lances with no pennons, on dark bay and brown horses. The background is only the beach, sea and laterite bluff with palms. Raza is frowning in his green high-wrapped turban, with a pointed moustache, his sheet's goatee and the scar on his anatomical left cheek turned toward us. One hand rests at the front of a quilted Indian saddle, by a brass-capped hilt or pommel post that does not read as a Western horn. He rides a dark bay. The open sky upper left and upper centre holds both balloons clear of faces. Minor note: the troop wear crossed leather belts over their jamas.

v02 is acceptable, with minor notes. The setting is now right: open wet-sand beach, surf, a red-laterite bluff with coconut palms and no buildings. Nagoji is on model: rust-red turban with curls at the nape, clean chin (light comic shading only), thick curled moustache, a tiny flush gold ear stud, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots and talwar. He holds the reins in his left hand on the plain grey gelding, and the upper right has a large clear sky for the balloon. Minor continuity note: the small, distant awning at upper left on the bluff is a red cloth canopy on three or four poles with a row of standing spearmen. In 2.2 and 3.2 it is a cream one-pole awning with two seated figures. If the author wants, a later touch-up could turn it into a single cream cloth on one pole and remove the standing figures. v01 is still unacceptable: it has a stone fort, a domed sentry turret, a church town and a rocky shore.

v02 is acceptable. Raza Khan is unchanged from v01 and on model: olive-green high-wrapped turban, hawk nose, pointed moustache with his sheet's grey-streaked goatee, scar on his ANATOMICAL LEFT cheek facing the camera, tight jaw, eyes flicking up and away. His hand grips the spear soundly. The background is fixed. Small and hazy on the red-laterite bluff is a single cream cloth slung from ONE pole. Under it sit Varma (bare-headed, no crown or turban, bare-chested, cream-and-gold cloth, spear leaning by the pole) and Ramayyan (thin, plain white, palm leaves). The beach and sea show at lower right. There are no foot soldiers, no throne, no text and no frame border. Minor only: the cloth runs out to the right with no visible tie-off, and at this size Varma's hair knot reads at the back of his head. For lettering, the large clear sky across the upper right takes the off-panel balloon, with its tail to the right frame edge. The caption fits top-left or top-right, clear of the awning. v01 is still unacceptable: it has a throne, a fringed four-pole canopy, a crowned king, guards, green-turbaned foot soldiers and a frame line.

The round 3 fix landed. Ponnan's single narrow red cloth now lies over his RIGHT shoulder (our left, on his rein-hand side) and runs diagonally down to his left hip, and there is no red left on the far shoulder or under his raised arm. His open toothy grin is now a faint closed-mouth smile. Nothing else got worse: the inset still has its white border and thin black outline, his raised open hand is sound, he wears the plain dark-brown jacket and white mundu with a bare knee, rides the small dun pony, and the bare-headed Maravar sit their horses on the laterite bluff. The main scene is unchanged: Raza Khan rides away on the dark-bay horse with the quilted saddle (no horn). He looks back over his left shoulder with the X scar on his anatomical left cheek. He keeps the olive-green turban, goatee and pointed moustache as on his sheet, and his lips are parted mid-call. The background is open beach with palms and the bluff, with no buildings, ships or Europeans. The upper-right sky is clear for his balloon. Minor note, not a rejection: at heavy zoom the woven borders of the saddle cloth and green drape show small glyph-like ornament. At reading size they read as textile pattern, and they are the same as in v02. v02 is not acceptable as a backup because of the wrong-shoulder cloth and the toothy grin.

Acceptable with minor notes. Raza Khan leads in the single deep-green turban (scar on his anatomical left cheek, goatee, lance). The Madurai line wears white jamas and white turbans, on dark bay, brown and black horses (no greys) with quilted saddles and pennonless lances, spray flying. The bare-headed Maravar stream down the bluff on brown and dun ponies. There are no buildings, no text and no gore. Minor deviations: the troopers wear crossed leather chest straps and leather belts rather than plain cloth waistbands (they still read as Carnatic cavalry, not Travancore regulars). Several horses carry small white stars. Most Maravar are bare-chested rather than in short jackets. The line is already in the shallows rather than just reaching the waterline. The clear sky in the upper left takes the caption.

v02 is clean. Raza Khan's face is turned to the viewer's left, so his anatomical left cheek faces the camera, and the scar is on that cheek only. He has the deep-green turban and drape, hawk nose, pointed moustache and goatee. Every other rider wears a white turban and white jama on a dark bay, dark brown or black horse, with quilted saddles and lances without pennons. One lance tips steeply sideways. The heavy horses churn hock- and knee-deep in grey slurry, heads up and mouths open, while their riders haul on the reins. On the right, the bare-headed Maravar rider grins back from a dun pony that is darting clear in a spray of wet sand. Behind is the laterite bluff with palms, the picket line and cook fires. There is no fort or building, and no text. Open sky at upper right takes the caption. Minor notes: the awning on the bluff has two poles, not one. The horses read slightly more as plunging through the slurry than as sinking mid-turn. The Maravar rider wears boots. v01 is not acceptable: it has a fort-like structure on the distant hill and the scar fix had not been made.

v02 is clean. The setting is now the low-tide Malabar beach: wet sand with sheet water, surf, and the laterite bluff with palms. There is no dry scrub and no fort. Nagoji matches the bible: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, long curly hair, rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrist, broad red sash, sheathed talwar and boots. His right arm is flung out, his left hand is on the reins and his mouth is open as he calls out. He rides a plain dapple grey. On the left are the white-turbaned, white-jama Madurai riders on mud-spattered dark horses. On the right are the bare-headed Maravar in brown jackets and white mundus on dun ponies. Open sky across the top takes the balloon. Note only: his ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a stud. v01 is not acceptable: it shows dry scrubland with a hilltop fort.

The r3 fix worked on both points, and a pixel diff shows nothing else changed beyond normal regeneration noise. (1) The background riders at the far left are now Madurai lancers: knee-length white jama, plain white waistbands, high-wrapped white turbans, dark brown and dark bay horses, and bamboo lances with no pennons. There are no brown jackets and no red, and they now match the lancers in 4.2. (2) The red awning at the left of the bluff is gone, replacing it are spectators and palms. The one remaining awning is plain cream. Everything else from v02 is kept: Nagoji on the plain grey in the full commander look (rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrist, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, sheathed sword), thick curled moustache, clean chin with only faint shading. Ponnan is beyond him, a head lower, on the dun pony: bare-headed, curly hair, thick moustache, clean chin, short dark-brown jacket, red cloth on his anatomical right shoulder, white mundu, bare knees, eyes forward. Hands are sound. There is no text, no Europeans, no fort and no ship. The upper-right sky is large and empty, so both Ponnan lines fit there. Minor notes, not grounds for rejection: (a) the cream awning hangs between two poles rather than one, and it is a tiny background detail; (b) two of the lancers' dark horses still show small white forehead stars, which the edit asked to remove but the bible does not forbid; (c) Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop rather than a stud, noted only. v02 is not acceptable as a backup: its brown-jacketed background riders and two red awnings are the faults r3 fixed.

Clean and on beat. Low-tide Malabar beach with surf, a red laterite bluff and palms; no fort or buildings. Nagoji matches: rust-red turban, clean chin with light jaw shading, curled moustache, cream sleeves to the wrists, red sash, talwar, boots, on a plain grey with a padded cloth saddle. Ponnan has his sheet face: broad, curly, heavy moustache, stockier. He wears a dark-brown short jacket (it reads a little like a loose shirt), red cloth on his right shoulder and a white mundu, with bare legs, on a smaller dun pony and a head lower. His eyes slide toward Raza Khan, who is small in the background in a green turban on a sand-caked dark horse, hand raised scolding it. Note only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop. A thin 2px dark edge line runs around the frame; the panel border will cover it. Wide open sky across the upper centre and right for both balloons.

Round-1 faults are fixed: no ships, no fort tower, no green on anyone but Raza Khan. Raza matches his sheet: lean, hawk nose, pointed moustache with goatee, deep-green high turban and drape, white jama. His face is turned frame-left so the scar on his anatomical left cheek reads. He shakes his booted foot in a plain iron stirrup on a quilted cloth saddle, wet sand falling, on a dark-bay horse. The background Madurai riders all wear white turbans and white jamas on bay or dark-brown horses, with no greys. Minor, accepted: the troopers wear crossed leather straps and leather belts over the jama (the bible says plain waistbands), and two background horses have white blazes. Nagoji speaks from off panel left, where Raza is glaring. Clear sky upper left and upper right for both balloons.

Clean. The fortress is gone. The coast is surf, dark rocks and a red laterite bluff with palms, with no buildings or flags, and no black border. Close medium shot of Raza Khan: green turban, pointed moustache and goatee, the X-scar on his anatomical left cheek toward camera. He looks down frame-left with his eyes on his horse's sand-caked neck, a frown easing toward shame. Quilted cloth saddle, lance with no pennon, hands sound. Background riders wear white turbans and ride dark bay or black horses, with no greys. Consistent with 5.2 (same costume, same dark horse). Large open sky across the upper left for the two off-panel Nagoji balloons, with tails to the left edge.

Acceptable. The building and bell tower are gone. The bluff now carries palms, cook-fire smoke, a picket line and small white-turbaned figures. Plain bamboo lances stand stacked upright at left with no pennons (tips run out of frame), with quilted saddles and cloth bundles at their foot, no chests. The mixed line runs along the water's edge, alternating Madurai riders in white turbans and jamas on tall black or dark horses with bare-headed Maravar riders on smaller dun ponies. One Maravar rider wears an open short dark jacket and the other is bare-chested; both wear white mundus hitched up, with bare legs and feet, and glisten with sweat. Weak points, not rejected: the heat shimmer is barely visible; the Madurai riders look less sweat-soaked than the Maravars; the tiny far-bluff awning is a multi-pole canopy rather than the one-pole awning. Big open sky across the upper right for both captions.

Setting fixed. They sit in palm shade on the same beach: surf, a red laterite bluff with palms, a troop shelter with a cook fire and white-turbaned men, and tethered dark horses. No river, no inland hills, no fort. Nagoji squats on his heels on the left: rust-red turban, clean chin, curled moustache, cream sleeves to the wrists covering both forearms, red sash, talwar, boots, hands sound. Raza Khan sits on the right, turned toward him. He is sweat-beaded, with his green turban loosened and the tail hanging, the healed X-scar on his anatomical left cheek toward camera and a pointed moustache. He holds a dried bottle gourd at his chin with his face clear, and has no red smears. Notes: Nagoji's ear ornament is a hanging gold drop (note only). The first speaker (Raza) sits on the right, so the letterer should stagger the balloons: Raza's high in the open centre sky, tailed right, and Nagoji's below and left of it. There is clear sky and sea between the heads for both.

v02 is clean: Nagoji alone, squatting on his heels on wet low-tide sand, three-quarter view, talking with a raised explaining hand (five digits, sound). He has the rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots and sheathed talwar, a clean chin and a thick curled moustache. His ear ornament is a small flush gold stud. The laterite bluff and palms are in the background, and there is no fort or other figure. The upper half is open sky, enough for both lettering lines. Minor notes: the surf shows as low rolling breakers along the shore rather than one thin slanting sheet. His boots are ankle-high lace-ups, shorter than the mid-calf boots on his sheet. v01 is unacceptable: it has a fort on the headland, a seated audience in red and rust turbans and crashing breakers on rocks.

v02 is acceptable. Raza Khan faces left and wipes his brow with the deep-green turban tail. His mouth and the scarred left cheek are uncovered, and he matches his sheet: hawk nose, pointed moustache, goatee, green drape, white jama. The background troopers wear white turbans and carry pennonless lances on dark brown horses. The setting is the beach, laterite bluff, palms and awning, with no fort, and the upper-left sky is clear for both lines. Nagoji's cream-sleeved hand closes on a slim grey driftwood stick, no longer a log. Minor notes: the hand enters from the left edge, not the lower edge. With the thumb on the near side it reads anatomically as a left hand, not the right hand the prompt asked for, but the grip is sound at reading size. The stick is a little thicker than a thumb. The background riders wear crossed belts, where the bible gives the Madurai troop plain waistbands. The tiny awning on the bluff has corner poles, not a single pole. v01 is unacceptable: it has a fort on the headland, a painted border and a heavy log under a flat hand.

v02 is clean. It is a square, edge-to-edge overhead view of wet sand in the inked, painted style and warm tan palette. There is one straight horizontal groove across the middle, with the driftwood tip at its left end and a single fingertip at the left frame edge, no forearm. A lip of foam sits in the lower-right corner. There are no other marks or text, and the upper half is plain sand for the lettering. Minor note: the stick tip is whittled to a pencil-like point. v01 is photographic and off-style.

The r3 fix landed. v03 is a clean edit of v02. The upper curve that entered from the upper left is gone. A new upper curve now enters from the upper right edge, sweeps left and down toward the straight groove, and comes within a hand's width of it just left of centre (tip at about x 0.43). It hooks back up and away in a soft rounded tip. It is a true mirror image of the lower curve, which still starts at the lower right where the stick tip rests. The lower tip changed from v02's flat hairpin to a rounded turn that curls down and away from the groove. Neither curve touches the groove or the other curve. The figure now matches the mirror-pair layout of the drawing in 6.5: tips close to the line at one end with an outward hook, spreading wide toward the other end. Nothing else got worse. The inked style, warm tan wet-sand palette, horizontal straight groove (consistent with 6.3), pebbles, scallop shell, foam wash at the left and lower-right edges, and the slim driftwood stick all carry over unchanged. The stick enters from the lower right with a single fingertip at the right edge and no forearm. There is no text, no arrowhead, barb, crossbar or emblem, and nothing anatomical beyond the fingertip. The upper-left quarter and upper centre are plain sand, ample for the one off-panel line. The tail point is the right frame edge nearest the hand holding the stick. Notes only: (1) The 'does not run alongside' part landed only partly. Both curves still run nearly parallel to the groove for a short stretch, about a quarter of the width, before the hook. (2) The tips are tighter scroll-like curls than the gentle hooks in 6.5, but they turn about half a circle, not a spiral, and at inset size they read as two flanking grooves pinching toward the line, not as a trident or emblem. (3) In 6.3 the stick enters from the left and here from the lower right. This reads as a new stroke and is not an error. v02 stays rejected: its rotationally symmetric S-pair (upper curve from the upper left) does not match the mirror-pair drawing in 6.5.

v02 is acceptable. Nagoji crouches on the left, scoring the sand with a slim stick. He has the rust-red turban, a clean chin, a thick curled moustache, cream tunic and red sash, and his sleeves come down to both wrists. Raza Khan crouches on the right facing Nagoji, with the scarred left cheek toward the camera, pointed moustache, goatee, deep-green turban and drape, and white clothes. Both faces are clear, and both turbans sit inside the middle 60 percent of the width. The upper third is open sea and sky with room for three balloons between the insets. The drawing is now exactly three grooves: a straight line from near to far and two curves that bend in and hook outward with rounded tips. There are no arrowheads, and a thin sheet of foam softens the near end of the straight groove. Hands are sound. Notes only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a stud (author undecided). The beach shows dark rocks rather than the laterite bluff of 6.1 and 6.2. The foam reaches the foreground although the sea is behind the pair. His talwar hilt sits behind his hip. The 6.4 inset must be edited to match this drawing's mirror-pair layout. v01 is unacceptable for the arrow-like groove ends and the sleeve and boot faults fixed in v02.

Minor only: Raza Khan traces the sand map with a fingertip instead of only studying it, and the map is a simple loop-and-line, not obviously half-erased. Nagoji has faint shading on his jaw but his chin reads clean-shaven. Otherwise clean. Nagoji has his thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, rust-red turban, cream tunic and red sash, with forearms on his knees. Raza matches his sheet: green turban and drape, crossed scar on the visible anatomical left cheek, pointed moustache, goatee. The beach, rocks and surf match 6.5 and 7.2. No text, the hands are sound, and there is clear sky at upper centre and upper left for both lines.

v02 is clean on every hard check. Setting matches 6.5: wet sand, foam, black laterite rocks, sea, and a bluff with palms. There is no fort, crate or rail. Raza matches his sheet: deep-green turban, olive drape, scar on his anatomical left cheek turned to camera, pointed moustache and grey-flecked goatee. He is mid-rise, one knee down and a hand on the other knee, and his hands are sound. Nagoji matches too: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red shoulder cloth and broad sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar, clean chin and thick moustache. He is on the right beside his grey, face turned back toward Raza. The background riders all wear white turbans and white jamas, ride dark horses and carry lances without pennons. The upper sky is clear above both speakers. Minor notes, none disqualifying: (1) Nagoji's sleeves are rolled to mid-forearm, not down to the wrists as the PRE-GENERATION NOTE asks. His inner left forearm is turned toward the horse, so no brand shows and nothing wrong is drawn. (2) The grey is a dapple grey rather than a flat plain grey. This matches the grey in 7.4 v01. (3) Nagoji has already reached the grey and is leading it, rather than walking toward it. (4) The awning on the bluff is a small multi-post canopy, not clearly one-pole. (5) Raza looks out to the left as the note directs; the background horses are behind him. (6) His ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop (note only). (7) The driftwood map grooves are not visible. v01 is unacceptable: hilltop fort, crates and picket rails, green turbans on other men, and Raza standing with a spear instead of rising.

The round 3 fix landed. Every horse in the rear of the line now faces and moves right, the same way as the foreground riders. The line follows one continuous curve from the far left background to the near right foreground, with no horses facing each other. The second Maravar rider from the left is now bare-headed with black curly hair, and his grey head cloth is gone. Nothing else got worse. The inked line and flat watercolour style, the blue afternoon sky, the laterite bluff with palms, the awning and cook smoke, the black rocks, the continuous spray arc and the four large foreground riders all match v02. Madurai riders wear high white turbans and white jamas on dark horses, with quilted saddles and plain bamboo lances with no pennons. The Maravar ride bare-headed on dun ponies, seats are quiet and reins slack. There is no text, no European element, no sunset and no gore, and the hands and anatomy are sound. The upper right sky is wide and low-detail, with room for both captions. Minor notes, not grounds to reject: the small background awning on the bluff seems to stand on two poles, not one (it was the same in v02, which the fix said to keep). The line now reads more as a curving column galloping along the water's edge than a tight wheel, but the arc does carry the turn toward the viewer. v02 stays rejected because of the reversed rear horses and the grey head cloth, so there is no backup.

v03 (newest) is clean on the script beat. Varma is bare-headed with a bun, no turban or crest, has the Vaishnavite forehead lines, is bare-chested with one cream-and-gold cloth over his shoulder and gold necklaces, and stands at the edge of the one-pole awning. Ramayyan (thin, receding hair, white cloth) sits on his stool marking a palm leaf. Nagoji swings down from a grey: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, cream tunic, red cloth, sand-caked boots and trousers. There is no painted text and no painted balloons, and the upper-right sky is wide open for Varma's balloon. Minor faults left for the author: (1) Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold bead, not a flat stud, visible at print size. (2) Nagoji wears a thin gold bracelet on his left wrist (bible: no royal jewellery; a simple bangle is borderline). (3) Nagoji's red cloth is draped from the shoulder across his chest into the waist, not the sheet's broad waist sash. It still reads as his red sash. (4) Varma's bun sits at the back of his head, not clearly above his left ear. (5) The grey is dappled, not plain grey, and its head is cropped by the right frame edge. Backup v02 has the same figures, but its background shows a European-style fortified town with towers and sailing ships. That does not match the empty training beach of this sequence or the 'no ships' sea of 8.4.

v02 is acceptable and fixes the round 1 setting. It is the open laterite bluff top beside a cloth awning, with the beach, surf, palms and a palm-covered headland below under afternoon sky. There is no fort, building, ship, king or extra figure. Nagoji is right: rust-red turban, curls at the nape, clean chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrist, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar. He holds the reins in a sound right hand, the grey's head is at his shoulder, and he faces frame right toward the king off panel. His left hand is sound on the scabbard. No text. Minor notes: (1) The gelding is a dappled grey, while 7.4 shows a plain grey. 9.2 is also dappled, so this matches 9.2. (2) The awning shows two poles, not one (7.4 had several, so this is consistent enough). (3) Note only: the ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop. The big sky at upper centre and right (x 0.38 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.35) takes both balloons. v01 stays rejected (fort courtyard, throne pavilion, guards, bearded king).

Acceptable with minor notes. The high wide is over Varma's bare shoulder from behind. He is bare-headed, with the knot at the top left of his head (his left, as the note requires), the cream-and-gold cloth over his left shoulder and the edge of the gold bead necklace. The beach, troop and sea are below, and there is open sky at upper right for the balloon. Notes: (1) A silvery streak shows at Varma's right temple. The script asks for black hair, and 7.4 shows none. (2) The beach holds a large crowd of foot soldiers with crossed belts, spears and shields as well as the mounted line, so it reads more like a muster than the mixed line regrouping. The Maravar are shown as bare-headed men, mostly on foot. (3) One pale taupe horse, partly hidden among the riders at about (0.66, 0.62), matches the tone of 7.3's Maravar dun ponies, so I read it as a dun pony, not a forbidden grey. All the other horses are dark bay, brown or black. No text, no Europeans, no ships.

v02 is acceptable and fixes the round 1 setting. It is the bluff top under a cloth awning on a wooden pole. A rough wooden table holds palm-leaf bundles and a clay pot, with open sea, beach, rocks and palms below. There are no churches, fort, ships, barrels or rings. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, sharp features, receding curly hair, plain white cloth. He sits on a low stool, looks up at Nagoji and holds a stylus over a blank palm-leaf bundle (no marks). His hands are sound. Nagoji is in the commander look: rust-red turban, clean chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic, red sash, talwar, cream trousers, sandy boots. He turns his head down toward Ramayyan. Both faces show. No text. Notes: (1) Nagoji's sleeves are rolled to the elbow here, but they are down to the wrist in 8.1 a moment earlier. His inner LEFT forearm shows the brand as a pale, speckled, ridged patch about a hand's width above the wrist, with no letters, numerals or cross and no ch9 long scar, so it is within the bible. If the author wants the page consistent, an optional edit of v02 can roll both sleeves down to the wrists and keep everything else. (2) His expression is a hard scowl. (3) Note only: the ear ornament is a hanging gold drop. (4) Ramayyan wears sandals; his sheet is barefoot. The sky across the top centre and right (x 0.3 to 1.0, y 0.03 to 0.33) holds all three lines. Ramayyan's first balloon can go top centre, Nagoji's below it nearer his head, and Ramayyan's last to the right. v01 stays rejected (Goa harbour, churches, European ship).

Acceptable. It is a wide of the open sea from the bluff, with a deep-blue band at the horizon and no ships. Varma stands small at the edge of the shelter, seen from behind: bare head with the knot on his left (frame left, as the note requires), the cream-and-gold cloth over his left shoulder, gold necklace and armlets, cream mundu, and the spear held in a sound right hand. There is plenty of open sky for two balloons, and no text. Minor notes: (1) He is fully lit rather than in silhouette. (2) The shelter is a carved wooden post with a woven, fringed roof on a stone-paved terrace with a masonry parapet, a sturdier build than 7.4's rough poles and cloth canopy. It is still a woven cover on a wooden post on the bluff, so it reads as the same place, but the letterer or author may notice the difference.

Minor only. There is a tiny red cross-shaped stroke inside the white namam above the red centre drop. It is not lettering and is barely visible at print size. The moustache is slightly fuller than the bible's 'thin, waxed' wording but matches the V15 sheet's front view. He glances sideways toward frame right rather than looking square into the lens, which still reads as looking at Nagoji off panel. Everything else matches the sheet and the beach/field row: bare head, sleek black hair in a knot on his left side, no turban or crest, namam with red centre, pearl drop earrings, clean-shaven chin, gold necklaces at the bottom of the frame, and the cream-and-gold cloth over one shoulder. The open sky fits the bluff in 8.2 and 8.4. The whole upper left is clear sky with room for the VARMA balloon. There is no text, no painted balloon and no anachronism.

The round 3 fix landed on all three points. The seated grey-haired king and the carved gilt chair with red upholstery are gone, and the right third is now only bluff, beach, surf and open sea, so the king is off panel. The red, gold-fringed, patterned canopy is now one plain undyed cream sheet on a single rough pole tied with rope. The three spear guards at the left edge are gone, with palms and grass continued behind the pole. Nothing else got worse. Nagoji matches the sheet and the chapter 7 commander look: rust-red turban with curls at the nape, cream tunic, broad red sash, talwar, thick curled moustache and clean-shaven chin. He gives a small, readable bow. Both hands are sound and hang at his sides. The beach line keeps white high-wrapped turbans, a single green turban (Raza Khan) and bamboo lances without pennons on dark bay and brown horses, with no greys. There is no fort, ship, European figure, text or pseudo-text anywhere. The upper-right sky gives a large clear area for NAGOJI's line, well away from his face. Note only: his ear ornament is a small round gold bead that sits close to the lobe, between a stud and a short drop. This is not a reason to reject. v02 stays rejected (king, chair, red fringed canopy and guards), so there is no backup.

v03 (newest) is clean on the hard checks: Nagoji matches the commander sheet (rust-red turban, long curly hair, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud visible, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, boots). He is seen from behind on a dappled grey riding down the slope toward the wet sand. The mixed line waits with their horses side by side: white-turbaned Madurai lancers on dark bay or black horses, bare-headed Maravar men on dun or brown ponies. Surf is breaking on the incoming tide. There is no painted text, balloon, fort or anachronism, and the anatomy is sound. The open sky in the upper centre and right takes both captions without covering any face. Minor faults for the author: (1) the Madurai chargers are about the same height as the Maravar ponies, where they should read as taller and heavier; (2) Nagoji's slope is rocky with scrub, while the selected 9.1 shows a grassy slope (the beach and sea match); (3) the riders sit stiffly in one rank facing the viewer, rather than looking winded and 'catching their breath'. v02 is the same composition but puts forts on the headland, which neither 9.1 nor the script has, so it is the backup only.

Acceptable. The strip runs from the lower edge of the rust-red turban (kept inside the frame) to the moustache. The eyes look forward, the curly hair and thick curled moustache are right, and the face matches the commander figure on the sheet. The right third of the strip is a dark, plain wall, ideal for the weighted caption. Notes: the ear ornament is a hanging gold drop rather than a stud (note only; the author has not decided). The strip runs a little below the top of the moustache and shows all of it. The expression reads as a hard scowl more than anticipation. A thin painted brown border band runs along the bottom edge (about 2% of the height); crop it when placing the panel.

v02 is acceptable and fixes both round-1 faults. Both sleeves are down to the wrists, with no forearm skin and no brand, and there are no grey or white horses in the line. Every mount is black, dark bay or dark brown. What works: the dusk picket line under the palms, cook fires and tripod pots in the dark beyond, and Nagoji walking among the mounts in the full commander look (rust-red turban, clean chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar), with his right hand on a black horse's head. His hands are sound. Kanka bleeds in from the right through a smoky dissolve, with no frame: a black mare at full stretch over dark soil, with no rider, saddle or bridle, her mane and tail streaming. Clear sky runs across the top for both captions. Notes only: (1) The memory takes about 40% of the width rather than a third. (2) Kanka's far hind leg is painted pale and half-transparent inside the dissolve. (3) The camp men at the fires are small figures in dark jackets with low cloth headwraps that read a little like caps. (4) The wooden stave buckets at the posts are watering buckets, not barrels. (5) The ear ornament is a tiny gold stud or drop. v01 is not acceptable: it shows a ridged patch on his bare RIGHT forearm and grey or white horses in the line.

v02 is acceptable and fixes the round-1 background. It has no fort, tower, colonial building, ship or harbour. The scene is a Travancore horse camp just after sunset: a blue-violet sky with an orange glow low down, palms, thatched horse shelters, a rope picket line, and cook fires with small silhouetted figures beyond. The line holds only black, dun and dark bay horses, with no grey. Kayal matches her sheet: an ochre red-brown bay with black mane, tail and lower legs, a fine head, the quilted ochre pad and bridle. Her ears are forward and her head a little high, and she looks toward the viewer, standing apart at the end of the line. Her four legs are sound, with no white socks. Open sky across the top takes both captions. Notes only: (1) A tiny pale glint, about 4 by 8 px, sits in the forelock at about (0.855, 0.27). It reads as a highlight on the hair, not a star, but it can be touched out. (2) The third horse in the line is a darker reddish bay, in shadow and clearly darker than Kayal. (3) One dun horse in the line has a white hind sock. (4) The ground is pale sand with thatched shelters, while 9.4 shows canvas tents on dark soil; it is plausibly the same camp. v01 is not acceptable: it has a whitewashed fort with a domed tower, a tiled building, a harbour and grey horses.

Both round-3 fixes landed and nothing else changed. (1) The pale round puckered patch on his RIGHT forearm (image left, below the rolled sleeve) in v02 is fully painted out in v03, leaving plain skin. No brand shows on the left forearm from this angle, which the instruction allows. (2) The second sun-like disc with its starburst behind the palm trunks on the bluff (about 0.47 across, 0.29 down in v02) is gone, along with the smaller glow near it. That spot is now dusky palm fronds against the orange sky, so the only sun is the disc on the sea horizon at the left. Everything that worked in v02 is kept. Nagoji has his commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic with rolled sleeves, broad red sash, talwar at his left hip, cream trousers and boots. He has the thick curled moustache and a clean chin. His ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop rather than a stud (noted only, not a reason to reject). The picket line mixes dun and dark-brown ponies with dark bay, dark brown and black horses. Kayal stands at the right end: an ochre red-brown bay with black mane, tail and lower legs, no white markings, and no other red-bay horse near her. The background grooms wear white turbans. The light is dusk, matching the neighbouring panels. The setting is beach, laterite bluff, palms and cook fires, with no fort, ship or European figure and no painted text. The open sky at upper left is clear for both captions. Minor points, not reasons to reject: the red awning on the bluff top is held up by several poles rather than one, but it is tiny and far in the background. A few background horses (not Kayal) have small white face markings or socks, and one or two legs behind the dun pony are hard to read.

v02 is acceptable. The setting matches 10.1: dusk, sun setting on the sea at left, laterite bluff with palms, cook fires, and the timber picket rail with horses behind it. Nagoji has the correct face: thick curled moustache, clean chin (faint ink stubble texture on the jaw only), rust-red turban on and wrapped as on the sheet, sleeves down to the wrists, right hand out palm up and low, left arm hanging. Kayal is ochre red-brown with a black mane and no white markings, nostrils at his palm. There is clear sky above, between his turban and her ears, for the balloon. Minor notes: (a) the talwar hangs at his RIGHT hip (image left), whereas 10.1 and 10.5 and the sheet put it at his left hip, a small prop continuity slip; (b) the ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop (noted only); (c) one plain grey horse at the rail behind, which reads as Nagoji's grey gelding, not a Madurai grey. v01 is unacceptable: bright midday, a watchtower with a guard, and a palisade.

v02 is acceptable. It is set on the beach picket line at sunset: rail fence, coconut palms, the sea, a plain headland and a cook fire. That matches the chosen 10.1, 10.2, 10.4 and 10.5. It also fixes the daylight fort that got v01 rejected (v01 is not offered in this round). The beat is right. Kayal's muzzle presses into Nagoji's chest, his near hand rests on her upper neck under the black mane, and his eyes are closed with his face against her forehead. Nagoji is on model: rust-red turban, curls at the nape, thick curled moustache, cream tunic with sleeves rolled, broad red sash and talwar. The inner left forearm faces the horse, so the brand is correctly not shown. Kayal matches her sheet: ochre red-brown bay, black mane, no white markings, ochre quilted pad and brass-fitted bridle. The hand and arm anatomy are sound. There is no text, pseudo-text, gore or anachronism. Note 1: his ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not the flush stud the bible asks for. This is the known ch1-8 deviation from the nagoji-v2 reference, it matches the drop in 10.2 and 10.4, and it goes on the author's deviation list. It is not a reason to reject. Note 2: faint stubble shading on the chin and jaw, within the light-stubble tolerance and invisible at print size. For lettering, the open sunset sky across the top centre (above the horse's ears, between the palms, about x 0.30-0.80, y 0.02-0.14) and the upper right sky (about x 0.70-0.95, y 0.12-0.30) take both captions clear of the faces and hands.

Acceptable with notes. A close two-shot at sunset with his turban touching her forehead, the last light on her ochre red-brown coat and black forelock, no white markings, and a sound hand holding the noseband ring. Identity is correct (commander face, rust-red turban, curls, thick curled moustache) and there is a wide dark sky across the top for all three lettering lines. Notes: a small blurred domed sentry turret at the far right edge (about x 0.95 to 0.99, y 0.52 to 0.68) reads faintly European; crop it out at placement if possible. Light stubble texture on the jaw. The ear ornament is a small hanging drop rather than a stud (noted only).

v02 is acceptable. The scene is dusk on the open beach, with the sun setting on an empty sea horizon at right, palms, the bluff with a cloth awning and cook fires at left, and no fort, watchtower, palisade or people. Kayal (left) has her head thrown high, black mane flying, mouth closed and natural, an ochre red-brown coat and no white markings. Nagoji has a quiet near-smile, thick curled moustache, clean chin, rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash and talwar at his left hip, and holds the reins in his right hand. His left sleeve is rolled up and shows a pale ridged scar patch on the left forearm. It sits a little higher than a hand's width above the wrist and on the outer face more than the inner, and it is not letters or a clean cross, so it is acceptable. There is a large clear sky area at upper right for both captions. Note: the ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop (noted only). The sun is on the right here and on the left in 10.1 and 10.2, which reads as a reverse angle. v01 is unacceptable: midday, a stone fort across the water, a watchtower, a palisade, and guards in crossed belts.

Acceptable with minor notes. Dusk over a stockade, palms and sea, with Nagoji alone with Kayal and his right hand on her neck. Commander look is correct: rust-red turban, curls at the nape, thick curled moustache, clean chin, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers and boots. Kayal is bay with black mane, tail and lower legs and no white markings. Notes: (1) Nagoji fills the strip's height rather than standing 'small in a large frame'. (2) No other horses are visible, so the 'line' reads as a palisade fence, which is acceptable because they are at the end of the line. (3) The talwar hangs on his right hip. (4) The ear ornament is a small hanging drop; note only. (5) His face sits in the upper quarter of the frame, but the frame was generated at the placed 3:1 shape, so it should not need a crop. There is no painted text and nothing European. The sky across the upper centre and right is wide and low-detail, with room for both captions.

v02 is clean. The ships and fort are gone. The setting is the beach at sunset with dark rocks, a palisade, the awning on the bluff with cook fires, and one small dugout. Nagoji is on-model: rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrist, red sash, cream trousers, boots and talwar. Kayal is bay with a black mane and black lower legs and no white markings. Ibrahim faces screen left with arms folded, so his lit left cheek and the scar from ear to jaw read. He wears a white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat, pocketed vest and white mundu. Notes only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a stud. His right arm passes behind Kayal's head and the hand rests on her neck at the mane line, not flat on the near side as the correction asked, but it reads as his hand on her neck. The awning on the bluff has more than one pole. Clear sky upper left and upper centre has room for both balloons. v01 is still unacceptable: masted ships and a stone structure on the headland.

v02 is acceptable. The setting is the dusk picket line on the laterite bluff: a palm, a rough stockade, dark tethered horses, a cook fire and the darkening sea, with no harbour, buildings, ships or crates. In the background, troopers wear white turbans and white jamas and carry a plain spear with no pennon. Ibrahim matches his sheet: arms folded, hands sound, white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over the pocketed vest, white mundu, and the scar from his left ear to his jaw lit, facing screen left. Nagoji appears from behind at the left foreground in the rust-red turban with curls at the nape, cream tunic and red sash. Notes only: Nagoji's visible jaw has a faint stipple that could read as very light stubble, but there is no beard and his chin is not shown. The sky is deeper post-sunset blue than in panels 2, 4 and 5, where the sun is still on the horizon. This is a small lighting step and acceptable. Open dark-blue sky between the two heads, upper centre, has room for three balloons. v01 is unacceptable: a daylight harbour with ships, warehouses, porters and crates, and a bearded Nagoji.

v02 is clean. The setting is the dusk beach and picket line: palms, a rough stockade, the cloth awning with cook fires, rocks and surf, and dark palm-covered headlands, with no fort, church, tower or buildings. The half-shrug reads: his left hand is out palm-up with a sound five-digit hand, his head is tilted, and he gives a wry half-smile toward screen right where Ibrahim stands off panel. His right hand rests in Kayal's black mane at the poll. Nagoji is on-model: rust-red turban with curls at the nape, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, a tiny flush gold ear stud, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrist, red sash and talwar. Kayal is bay with a black mane and no white markings on her face. A large clear sky at upper right has room for the one long balloon. v01 is unacceptable: daylight, a stone rampart with guards and spears, and a European fort and palace on the far shore.

v02 is clean. Ibrahim is alone, shoulder against a palm on the laterite bluff, with a stockade and dark tethered horses behind him. His quiet gaze goes screen left over the darkening sea, with the last orange band at the horizon. There are no ships, quay, buildings, torches or town lights. He is on-model: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over the vest with bulging pockets, white mundu, hands behind his back, and his left cheek turned to camera so the scar from ear to jaw reads. Clear sky at upper left has room for the one long balloon. v01 is unacceptable: a night harbour with a stone quay, bollards, crates, a tiled building, a torch, ships and town lights.

v02 is clean. It is dusk at the palm picket line with a cook fire, white-turbaned Travancore men and a cloth awning on the bluff, and there are no buildings, ships or Europeans. Ibrahim matches his sheet (white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal coat over a pocketed vest). His hand is flat on the trunk and he half turns toward the sea at left, with the scar visible on his anatomical left cheek. Nagoji has a clean chin, curled moustache and full commander kit. One hand is on Kayal's neck, the other hangs at his side, and his sleeves are down. Kayal is a plain bay with no face markings and black points. Note only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging drop. Kayal's long mane hangs very low beside her chest, which is minor. The upper sky between and above the heads is free for the balloon. v01 is rejected because it shows a church or fort on the headland and a ship.

Clean pick. It is dusk beyond the palms, the backwater channel meets the sea with pale surf folding into dark still water, and the three figures sit together at the left edge. Kayal is bay with a black mane and black lower legs and no white markings. Ibrahim's costume matches his sheet. Nagoji is in the full commander look with a clean chin. The boats are small local lateen craft with thatched huts, with nothing European. The large empty sky upper right holds the long balloon easily. Notes only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging drop. Ibrahim is seen mostly from behind, so his scar does not show, which this wide does not require. They stand on a rocky outcrop above the channel, which fits the elevated picket line of 11.1.

v02 is clean. It is the dusk beach and picket line: the sea and sunset behind, a palm at right, and white-turbaned Travancore regulars with crossed belts and spears by a cook fire. There is no wall, harbour, ship or building. Ibrahim pushes off from the palm with his hand on the bark. He faces Nagoji at frame left, so his anatomical left cheek and the ear-to-jaw scar face the camera. Both hands are sound. Nagoji's rust-red turban, curls and sash-draped shoulder are seen from behind at the left edge. His ear ornament is a hanging drop (note only). The second face entry is the back of Nagoji's head, listed only so balloons stay off it. The sky from about x 0.2 to 0.5 and y 0 to 0.4 holds two stacked balloons. v01 is rejected for the stone harbour wall, barrels, ship and fort.

The R3 fix landed. In v02 Ibrahim looked ahead over his right shoulder toward frame right, so the scarred side was hidden. In v03 he looks back over his LEFT shoulder (the frame-left side, where the striped shawl hangs) toward Nagoji and Kayal, in near profile facing frame left. His mouth is open as he speaks and his white turban catches the orange light. Nothing else changed from v02 and nothing got worse: same beach, laterite bluff with palms, surf and sunset; Nagoji from behind in rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, sleeves to the wrist and talwar; Kayal's plain bay head with black mane and no white markings; footprints in the wet sand. There are no ships, buildings, Europeans or painted text. Minor: at this distance Ibrahim's left-ear-to-jaw scar is not legible in the art. His face is the correct side toward camera, and beard, turban, teal short coat and shawl match his sheet. Note only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop rather than a stud. His chin is not visible because he is seen from behind. The clear dusk sky in the upper right (about x 0.50 to 1.0, y 0.0 to 0.30) takes the single IBRAHIM balloon above his head without covering a face or the action. v02 stays rejected: Ibrahim's speaking face is turned away from Nagoji, so the scar does not read.

v02 fixes the setting. At left is a low laterite bluff with coconut palms, and the far headland is plain and palm-topped. There is no castle, tower or shore light, and nothing anachronistic. The night sea lies under a full moon with its reflection. The line of hoofprints filling with water runs across the wet sand at lower left. Nagoji has a clean chin, curled moustache, and the full commander kit with laced boots and talwar. One hand is on Kayal's cheek and the other holds the scabbard, both sound. His sleeves are rolled to the elbow, but no forearm mark is visible. Kayal is bay with a black mane, tail and lower legs. Notes only: (1) a short pale moonlight glint runs down the front ridge of Kayal's forehead. It is far smaller and softer than v01's stripe and reads as a rim highlight from the moon at right, but if the author reads it as a marking, a one-touch retouch to bay brown fixes it. (2) Nagoji's ear ornament is a hanging drop. (3) Heads sit slightly above the middle half of the height, but the frame is already generated at the 3:1 placed ratio, so no crop is needed. The wide dark sky across the upper left and centre holds all three captions. v01 is rejected for the castle and towers on the bluff and the headland.
